translation.english_title: Dark machaan, this is for you

english_lines: Dark machaan, this is for you — aa...
I've kept fried fish ready — mm... mm...
Open your mouth and take it — I
Will spread the mat and lie down — mm... mm...
You leap over and hold me,
Don't shrink away and stand there; run over and lean into me,
notes: `மச்சான்` remains `machaan`, preserving the intimate colloquial kin/lover address.
The food, mat and bodily invitation remain direct rather than being euphemized.

english_lines: O fire that has caught hold of me,
I am an aandi — don't prod me and pull me.
notes: `பச்சரிசி சிரிப்பு` remains the source-shaped `raw-rice smile` image.
`ஆண்டி` remains `aandi` rather than being narrowed to one English religious/social label.

english_lines: Hey... it is the aandi who needs six-time puja,
Don't look at this `naanumuttha pora mezhugu`.
notes: The verified compact phrase `நானுமுத்த போற மெழுக` is not silently segmented or repaired from an external lyric. It remains transliterated as a documented pressure point.
The teasing insult remains sharp and colloquial.

english_lines: You put on an ascetic disguise,
notes: The verified `அடுப்பதும் பொண்ணுன்னு` is retained as `adupathum ponnu` because a smooth explanatory rendering would require choosing an unprinted syntactic repair.
The explicit demand that men reform and slavery end is retained, as is `thaali` rather than a generic wedding-token substitute.

english_lines: Hey... if I eat fried fish,
Don't ruin me by putting asaivam before me.
notes: `சைவம் / அசைவம்` is retained as `saivam / asaivam` so the vegetarian/non-vegetarian wordplay remains available for the woman's reply.
`சாமிகுத்தம்` remains `saami-kutham`, preserving the colloquial religious-fear register.

english_lines: The bond of man and woman —
Don't reject the fish that comes near you.
notes: `அசைவம்` carries both the food opposition and a bodily/movement suggestion; it remains `asaivam` rather than being reduced to one English sense.

english_lines: That is how I too, machaan,
notes: The Yama-vehicle insult is preserved rather than replaced by a generic animal insult.
The verified closing `உன்மனசும் எங்களையா` is rendered conservatively; the Tamil witness is not altered to resolve its colloquial grammar.

translator_notes: This two-page duet mixes sexual teasing, food/vegetarian wordplay, colloquial insults and a direct anti-subordination demand. The English keeps that instability instead of sanitizing it into romantic banter.
Full source provenance remains PDF 121–122 as one translation record.
This is a literary source-faithful translation, not a singable adaptation.
